teaser: Every image model on OpenRouter, eleven briefs, 101 images judged blind, $10.44: which model for which infographic, and what it costs.
core_idea: To make infographics part of the newsroom's workflow, every image-output model on OpenRouter on 10 October 2026 was given the same briefs from one article, from 18 words to 2,800, plus an edit, a component, a brand slide and a deck, over five rounds with blind judging and recorded costs; the answer is to choose the model by the job, not the budget: Nano Banana 2.1 for concept slides, charts and decks, Gemini 3 Pro Image when speed matters, GPT-5.4 Image 2 for documents, edits, components and brand slides, with prompt rules learned from the faults and a style reference for every deck.

figures.caption: The bake-off's conclusion, drawn by the model it recommends for this job (GPT-5.4 Image 2, given the conclusion as a 263-word document). The blind judge scored it 9 out of 10 and would publish it as it is.

The same diagram brief for all ten contestants, with the blind score. Two models ignored the requested 16:9 and returned a square that cut off boxes at both ends; one painted a muddy gradient; one misspelled three words.
Fourteen exact numbers. Five models got every value and proportion right; GPT-5 Image wrote "artitty" for artefact, three wrong values, three missing bars and a claim bar a third too short.
The edit. GPT-5.4 Image 2 added a sixth box and kept the other five. Gemini 3 Pro changed the title and the colour, and made room for the new box by replacing the last one: "canary report" is gone.
Nano Banana 2.1, slides 2 and 3 without and with slide 1 attached as a style reference. The top bar, the kicker and the headline type carry through.
Quality against price for every model. The three recommended sit on the frontier; Gemini 3.1 Flash is beaten by Nano Banana 2.1 on both axes; GPT-5 Image is the most expensive and the worst.
